To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a DRT in combination with spray skin/autologous skin grafts can reduce the donor site burden and time to complete reepithelialization when compared with similar defects treated with DRT/autologous grafts alone.

the use of a dermis‐based DRT in conjunction spray skin/STGS can reduce donor site morbidity and decrease time to healing, and that the use of this combination may also permit greater meshing ratios, and improved re‐pigmention, when compared with similar wound defects treated with a DERT and autologous STSG alone.

using a dermal regenerate in conjunction with spray‐on skin and autologous split skin grafting reduces donor site burden and decreases time to complete re-epithelialization in comparison with similar wounds treated using the dermal regenerate template alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of spray epidermal skin in conjunction with a DRT in the treatment of complex, full‐thickness skin wounds.
the development and evaluation of a novel, minimally invasive, autologous cell therapy for the treatment of full‐thickness soft‐tissue defects.
a pilot study of the use of a DRT in combination with a spray skin/STSK in the treatment of full‐thickness defects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a DRT in combination with a spray skin and STSG is an effective treatment for full‐thickness soft‐tissue defects.

the DRT in conjunction to the spray skin technology and STSG can reduce donor sites burden and decrease the time to complete healing, as well as permit larger or greater meshing ratio, while aiding in re‐pigmentation.
the combination of DRT, spray skin and STSG can be used to treat large soft tissue defects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new treatment paradigm for complex full‐thickness soft‐tissue loss that combines the use of a DRT, spray skin technology and split‐thickness autologous skin to achieve improved outcomes in a more timely fashion with less donor site burden and complications.
the combination of spray skin, DRT and STG can be used to restore large full‐thickness defects.
spray skin technology can reduce the donor site burden and improve the outcomes of patients with full‐thickness soft‐tissue defects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a DRT in addition to spray skin and autologous split skin grafting can reduce the donor site burden and improve the cosmetic outcome of full‐thickness soft‐tissue defects.

the use of spray on skin as an adjunct to dermal regenerative template and split thickness skin grafting can reduce donor site morbidity and improve outcomes in the treatment of large full thickness defects.

using a dermal regenerate matrix in conjunction with spray epidermal skin can decrease donor site burden and time to complete re-epithelialization when compared with DRT and split thickness grafting alone.
